WITH team_half_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    team_id,
    CASE 
      WHEN w IS NOT NULL AND g IS NOT NULL AND g > 0 
      THEN CAST(w AS FLOAT) / g 
      ELSE NULL 
    END AS win_rate
  FROM manager_half
),
team_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    team_id,
    AVG(win_rate) AS avg_win_rate,
    COUNT(win_rate) AS record_count
  FROM team_half_stats
  GROUP BY team_id
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_win_rate) AS mean_avg_win_rate
  FROM team_averages
)
SELECT 
  ta.team_id,
  ta.avg_win_rate,
  ta.record_count,
  ta.avg_win_rate - om.mean_avg_win_rate AS difference
FROM team_averages ta, overall_mean om
ORDER BY 
  difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The "record count" requested refers to the count of valid manager_half records (where w and g are both non-NULL and g > 0) that contributed to each team's average win rate, not the total count of all manager_half records for that team.

Teams appearing in manager_half but having no valid records (all records with NULL w or g, or g=0) are included in results with NULL average, record_count=0, and NULL difference, sorting to the end of the result set.

alternatives.interpretation: If "record count" should reflect the total count of all manager_half records for each team (regardless of validity), use COUNT(*) instead of COUNT(win_rate) in the team_averages CTE.
